By Mohammad Faisal ,
1 hours ago
The NBA trade deadline 2026 once again delivered blockbuster surprises across the league. But even for a veteran like LeBron James, one particular deal stood out as completely unexpected.
In a deadline filled with headline moves, including James Harden landing with the Cleveland Cavaliers and Anthony Davis moving to the Washington Wizards, it was the trade involving Jaren Jackson Jr. that caught the NBA‚Äôs all-time leading scorer off guard.
LeBron James Surprised By Jaren Jackson Jr.‚Äôs Move to Utah Jackson Jr. was traded to the Utah Jazz on February 3, 2026, in a massive eight-player deal just before the deadline. The Memphis Grizzlies received Walter Clayton Jr., Kyle Anderson, Taylor Hendricks, Georges Niang, along with three future first-round picks.
The move gives Utah a major defensive anchor and playoff-tested frontcourt presence, adding the 2023 Defensive Player of the Year to a young and athletic core.
Speaking on the latest episode of the Mind the Game podcast with Steve Nash, James explained why the trade stood out to him.
‚ÄúThey [Utah Jazz] have a lot of athleticism, you know, with the rookie [Ace] Bailey. Obviously, Keonte George is playing exceptional basketball this year‚Ä¶ Now you add Jaren Jackson who‚Äôs battle tested as well, been in playoff games. Of course they‚Äôre trying to build something I think for the next couple years.‚Äù
‚ÄúObviously, you know, they haven‚Äôt played how they would like to play. Obviously, their big fell has been out pretty much all year. Walker Kessler has been out all year.‚Äù
‚ÄúBut you can imagine signing that front court of Jaren Jackson Jr. That‚Äôs length.‚Äù
‚ÄúSo, it was that was an interesting trade. I didn‚Äôt see that coming. There were talks of Jaren Jackson, you know, not being a part of the Memphis Grizzlies future, but I didn‚Äôt see it being Utah and going there and doing that. But, listen‚Ä¶ they got a billion first round picks and picks locked up, so they can pretty much do anything. It‚Äôs like they play Monopoly at this point.‚Äù
Jackson Jr. has continued to produce at a strong level during the 2025‚Äì26 season, averaging 19.4 points, 5.7 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.1 steals, and 1.4 blocks per game while shooting 47.6% from the field and 35.7% from three-point range. His ability to stretch the floor while protecting the rim makes him one of the most versatile two-way big men in the league.
Since arriving in Utah, Jackson Jr. has already shown flashes of impact. In his early appearances with the Jazz, he has averaged 22.3 points, 4.3 rebounds, and 2.7 assists across three games, helping the team go 2‚Äì1 during that stretch.
Despite the addition, Utah remains in a rebuilding phase. The Jazz currently hold a 13‚Äì38 record and are sitting near the bottom of the conference standings. However, the organization clearly views Jackson Jr. as a foundational piece moving forward, especially alongside young talents like Keonte George and Walker Kessler.
For James, the surprise wasn‚Äôt that Jackson Jr. was traded; it was where he landed. With Utah holding significant draft capital and a developing roster, the move signals a long-term vision that could reshape the franchise over the next few seasons.
